title: Coordinate-face base change for an unpunctured full root tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ use all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart, and $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ a reduced strict normal crossings boundary whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale and put
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\leq d\leq r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right).$$
The index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility, with transition $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a profinite set $P$ let $T[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_a}\coprod_{P_a}T$, and let $\mathcal N_P$ be the pullback of $\mathcal N$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].
Write $q_P:T[P]\to U$ for the structural map. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(t_j)_{j\in J})$, with closed inclusion $g_J:U_J\hookrightarrow U$, and put
$$T_J=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}(R/(t_j)_{j\in J})[x_{d,n}]_{d\notin J}/(x_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)_{d\notin J}\right).$$
Let $e_J:T_J\to T$ set all roots indexed by $J$ to zero; let $q_{J,P}:T_J[P]\to U_J$ be structural and $e_{J,P}:T_J[P]\to T[P]$ the induced map. Use closed inverse/direct-image adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Define $\beta_{J,P}$ to be the adjunct of
$$q_P^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\longrightarrow\mathcal N_P[0]$$
after pulling the counit back by $e_{J,P}$ and identifying $q_{J,P}^*g_J^*=e_{J,P}^*q_P^*$. Then
$$\beta_{J,P}:g_J^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R(q_{J,P})_*e_{J,P}^*\mathcal N_P[0]$$
is an isomorphism. Equivalently it is the usual cartesian exchange followed by restriction from $T\times_UU_J$ to $T_J$; the latter map is the surjective closed immersion killing all the nilpotent roots indexed by $J$. The adjunct back on $U$ is exactly $Rq_{P,*}$ of the closed unit for $e_{J,P}$, with the canonical composition identification. The comparisons agree for $J\subseteq J'$ with successive coordinate restriction and are compatible with restriction to open subsets of $U$. They are natural in $P$, in maps of the supplied lisse modules, and under pro-etale base change of $U$, and commute with root-tower automorphisms preserving these faces and with the supplied module actions. For a profinite family indexed by $Q$, compatibility is equality on the $Q$-parametrized terms. The cases $J=\varnothing$, $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, rank zero and empty charts are included. There is no puncture, outer/inner partition, or closed union in this assertion.

proof.text: Write $S$ for the displayed full tower algebra. The quotient of $S/(t_j)_{j\in J}$ by all $x_{j,n}$, $j\in J$, is exactly the displayed algebra of $T_J$: in the quotient presentation the relations for $j\in J$ become $0=0$, and the other relations and transition maps are unchanged. Every $x_{j,n}$ in $S/(t_j)$ is nilpotent since its $n$th power is zero. Every element of the ideal they generate is a finite sum of multiples of finitely many such roots and is therefore nilpotent. Thus $T_J\to T\times_U U_J$ is a surjective closed immersion, without a uniform nilpotence bound. For finite quotients $P_a$, finite products give the same quotient calculation on $\coprod_{P_a}T$; passage to the colimit gives it on $T[P]$. In particular the closed complement of $e_{J,P}$ is the finite union of the opens $D(t_j)$, so is quasi-compact.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal W$ be the class of affine $W$ ind-etale over $U_J$ with w-contractible coordinate ring. Every object of $(U_J)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ is covered by members of $\mathcal W$: cover it by affines; each affine $V$ is weakly etale over $U_J$, so it has a faithfully flat ind-etale $V'\to V$ with $V'$ ind-etale over $U_J$; cover $V'$ by w-contractible $\operatorname{Spec}D_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subset V'$ with $B_i\to D_i$ ind-etale; an affine open immersion of affines is etale of finite presentation, so $D_i$ is ind-etale over $U_J$ by composition. For $W\in\mathcal W$ put $A_W=v(W)$ in the affine ind-etale basis over $U$. The closed-site functor gives $W=A_W\times_UU_J$ as a closed immersion, and every point of $A_W$ specializes to $W$. Since $(\Gamma(A_W,\mathcal O),I)$, $I$ generated by the $t_j$, $j\in J$, is a henselian pair and its quotient is the w-contractible coordinate ring of $W$, the ring $\Gamma(A_W,\mathcal O)$ is w-contractible. Both $W$ and $A_W$ are weakly contractible. The complement of $U_J$ is $\bigcup_{j\in J}D(t_j)$, quasi-compact, and $U$ is affine; so for every module sheaf $H$ the actual closed unit identifies $(g_J^*H)(W)$ with $H(A_W)$. Evaluations at $W$ and $A_W$ are exact. Hence for a complex $K$ on $U_J$ and $W\in\mathcal W$, $\mathcal H^q(K)(W)=H^q(K(W))$; a sheaf vanishing on all members of $\mathcal W$ vanishes, since its sections on any object inject into the product over such a cover. Thus a map of complexes on $U_J$ whose evaluations at all $W\in\mathcal W$ are quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text:
Put $A=\Gamma(A_W,\mathcal O)$, $X=T[P]\times_U A_W$ and $X'=T_J[P]\times_{U_J}W$. The coordinate algebra of $X$ is the directed colimit, over $n$ and finite quotients $P_a$, of
$$\prod_{P_a} A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_d^n-t_d)_d.$$
Every factor has finite presentation and is generated as an $A$-module by the monomials $\prod_d x_d^{e_d}$ with $0\leq e_d<n$: reduce each exponent by its monic relation. A finite product is again a finite finitely presented $A$-algebra, by adjoining its finitely many orthogonal idempotents to the presentations of the factors. Similarly $X'$ has finite stages with $t_j=0$ and only the variables $d\notin J$. Adjoin the finitely many relations $t_j=0$ to see finite presentation over $A$, and use the same monomial generating lists for finiteness. The ring $A$ is w-contractible by step 2. Apply the ind-finite algebra lemma to both systems. Thus $X$ and $X'$ are w-strictly local, and every closed point of $X$ maps to a closed point of $A_W$.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.9 (cofiltered limits of w-local spectral spaces) and Example 2.2.2 (limits along w-local maps preserve w-strict locality); finite-stage input Stacks proetale.tex Tag 0986, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-over-w-contractible. Agent-extracted combined algebraic formulation.

proof.text: Every closed point of $A_W$ lies in $W$, by the specialization assertion in step 2. Thus at each closed point of $X$ every $t_j$, $j\in J$, vanishes in the residue field; the relation $x_{j,n}^n=t_j$ forces every $x_{j,n}$ to vanish there. Consequently the closed immersion $h:X'\hookrightarrow X$ contains every closed point of $X$. A closed subspace containing all closed points has exactly the same closed points: a point which is not closed has its distinct closed specialization still in that subspace. Since $X$ and $X'$ are w-local, their closed-point spaces are their component spaces, with the actual subspace and quotient topologies. Hence $\pi_0(h)$ is a homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 096A (definition-w-local), the following closed-points/components description, and Tag 096B (lemma-closed-subspace-w-local). The root equations identify the relevant closed points explicitly.

proof.text:
The restriction $L=\mathcal N_P|_X$ remains finite-rank lisse: pull a trivializing cover back, and pull its finite free trivializations back. The w-strict component-cohomology theorem, applied to $h:X'\to X$ and $C_F$, gives that the actual restriction
$$R\Gamma(X,L[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X',h^*L[0])$$
is an isomorphism. Its coefficient hypothesis is only that $C_F$ is a commutative condensed ring; in particular it applies to all continuous $\Omega$-valued functions for the incomplete extended norm topology, with no reduction to finite-valued functions or to finite coefficient fields.

source.place: Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3, equation (4.2), and Corollary 4.7, extended by descent from w-contractible to w-strictly local affines using Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.2.8. This w-strictly local extension is agent-formulated, not a verbatim assertion of Proposition 4.3.

proof.text: These are precisely the evaluations of $\beta_{J,P}$ on $W$. Indeed use the exact section-module equivalences, which preserve the specified adjunctions and sections, and take a K-injective resolution $I$ of $\mathcal N_P[0]$. Direct image preserves K-injectives, so $Rq_{P,*}$ is represented by $q_{P,*}I$. By step 2, exact evaluation of $g_J^*q_{P,*}I$ at $W$ is the complex $I(X)$. Localization of derived sections identifies this complex with $R\Gamma(X,L[0])$. On the other side, evaluation at contractible $W$ of $R(q_{J,P})_*e_{J,P}^*\mathcal N_P[0]$ is $R\Gamma(X',h^*L[0])$ by the same argument. The inverse-image functors on the slices have the pulled-back coefficient rings, and localization identifies their small sites. Applying the defining counit of $q_P^*\dashv Rq_{P,*}$ and then transposing along $q_{J,P}$ gives restriction of sections from $X$ to $X'$: its transpose is the pulled-back counit on both sides. Thus the evaluated map is the specific map of step 5, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. Exactness of the covering tests now proves that $\beta_{J,P}$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category.

source.place: Tag 0D6F (lemma-unbounded-cohomology-of-open); K-injective evaluation together with proetale.tex Tags 09BK, 09BL. Adjunction identification is written out from the specified counit.

proof.text: For the cartesian square with $T[P]\times_U U_J$, the ambient exchange is by definition the transpose of the pulled-back counit. Follow it by the unit restricting from that fibre to $T_J[P]$. The composite has the same transpose as $\beta_{J,P}$; uniqueness of transpose gives equality. The latter closed immersion is surjective by step 1, so its pullback is an exact equivalence for condensed modules, and its adjunction unit is an isomorphism. This also justifies viewing the displayed comparison as the usual cartesian exchange followed by that restriction, despite the unbounded nilpotent ideal. Transpose $\beta_{J,P}$ instead under $g_J^*\dashv g_{J,*}$. Its further transpose under $q_P^*\dashv Rq_{P,*}$ is $e_{J,P}^*$ of the counit, whence it is exactly $Rq_{P,*}$ of the closed unit $\mathcal N_P[0]\to(e_{J,P})_*e_{J,P}^*\mathcal N_P[0]$, with the canonical composite direct-image comparison. The normalized derived-composition adjunction identifies these composite units and counits.

source.place: Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening), and the units/counits of the closed adjunctions. The two transpose computations are categorical consequences of the normalized composite adjunction.

proof.text: For $J\subseteq J'$ the two quotient homomorphisms set the roots of $J$ and then those of $J'\setminus J$ to zero. Their composite sets exactly the roots of $J'$ to zero. The transpose of the successive comparison is therefore the counit pulled back along this composite, equal to the transpose of $\beta_{J',P}$. The triangle identities and normalized derived composition give equality of these maps. The same computation applies after restricting to an open of $U$. For any pro-etale $U'\to U$, small-site localization identifies the restriction of $Rq_{P,*}$ with direct image for its base change: on a K-injective $I$ both are the section complexes $I(T[P]\times_U V)$ at a test $V\to U'$. Derived localization and the preserved adjunctions identify the maps as well. It follows that all the comparisons commute with such base change, not just that their source and target happen to be isomorphic.

proof.text: A map $P'\to P$ induces the corresponding maps of profinite test schemes and their section restrictions. Morphisms of the supplied modules commute with the counit, so transposition gives the naturality squares in both variables. Face-preserving tower automorphisms commute with the quotient maps; hence the same squares give equivariance, including the supplied module actions. For an action parametrized by $Q$, perform this construction on $T[P][Q]=T[P\times Q]$ and its face, using the action morphism there. Naturality of the actual counit gives equality there, so no inference from equality only at the points of $Q$ is needed. If $J=\varnothing$, the identity quotient and triangle identity give the identity comparison; if $J$ is all coordinates, the same argument has no remaining root variables. Finite free rank zero and empty spectra give the zero complexes throughout; $r=0$ has only $J=\varnothing$.
